title_en: Four Typical Cases of Drug Crimes by the Supreme People's Court
keywords_en: drugs; robbery; People's Court cases on drug crimes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Four Typical Cases on Drug Crimes

1. Xia Zhijun, He Pingquan, et al. — Manufacturing drugs, illegal possession of firearms

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Xia Zhijun, male, Han nationality, born March 4, 1978, unemployed. In March 2001, he was sentenced to four years' imprisonment for robbery, and was released upon completion of sentence on January 15, 2004.

Defendant He Pingquan, male, Han nationality, born June 1, 1984, farmer.

Defendant Xu Xiangping, male, Han nationality, born August 28, 1976, farmer. In May 1994, he was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for robbery, and was released upon completion of sentence in August 1997.

Defendant Yang Cuibin, male, Han nationality, born October 14, 1988, farmer.

Defendant He Fangming, male, Han nationality, born June 8, 1974, farmer.

Defendant Chen Yong, male, Han nationality, born June 14, 1984, farmer.

Defendant You Chao, male, Han nationality, born July 23, 1983, farmer. In March 2001, he was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for robbery, and was released upon completion of sentence on April 10, 2003.

Defendant Wang Ping, male, Han nationality, born November 4, 1976, farmer.

In March and April 2007, Defendants Xia Zhijun and He Pingquan conspired to manufacture ketamine. Xia introduced He to Defendant Wang Ping, the business supervisor of Chengdu Xinxin Ke Chemical Instrument Co., Ltd. in Sichuan Province, to purchase equipment and raw materials for drug manufacturing. In late April of the same year, He Pingquan purchased drug-manufacturing equipment and raw materials from Wang Ping, used the hydroxylimine provided by Xia Zhijun and the process taught by Xia, and hired Defendants Xu Xiangping, He Fangming, and Chen Yong to manufacture approximately 20 kilograms of ketamine at He's home in Longwang Town, Qingbaijiang District, Chengdu.

In early May of the same year, Defendant He Pingquan purchased drug-manufacturing raw materials from Defendant Wang Ping, used the hydroxylimine provided by Defendant Xia Zhijun, and hired Defendants Xu Xiangping, He Fangming, Chen Yong, and Yang Cuibin to manufacture approximately 20 kilograms of ketamine at Yang Cuibin's home in Fuhong Township, Qingbaijiang District, Chengdu.

In mid-May of the same year, Defendant He Pingquan purchased drug-manufacturing raw materials from Wang Ping, used the hydroxylimine provided by Defendant Xia Zhijun, and hired Defendants Xu Xiangping, He Fangming, Chen Yong, Yang Cuibin, and Defendant You Chao (introduced by Xia Zhijun) and Zhang Bo (already separately convicted and sentenced) to manufacture 37.138 kilograms of ketamine at He Fangming's home in Longwang Town, Qingbaijiang District, Chengdu. Xia Zhijun and He Pingquan transported these drugs to He's temporary residence for concealment, where they were later seized.

In late May of the same year, Defendant He Pingquan and Xu Xiangping leased a factory building in Longtan Township, Chenghua District, Chengdu. He Pingquan purchased drug-manufacturing equipment and raw materials from Wang Ping, used the hydroxylimine provided by Defendant Xia Zhijun, and Xu Xiangping organized Yang Cuibin, He Fangming, Chen Yong, You Chao, and others to manufacture ketamine in this factory. On the evening of June 2 of the same year, public security officers arrested He Pingquan, Xu Xiangping, He Fangming, Chen Yong, Yang Cuibin, and You Chao at the drug-manufacturing site, seizing on the spot 246.2 kilograms of ketamine, 1,018 kilograms of brown liquid containing ketamine, and drug-manufacturing equipment and raw materials. Later, based on He Pingquan's statement, public security officers recovered from his temporary residence one imitation Type 64 pistol and 14 rounds of ammunition. On December 4 of the same year, public security officers arrested Xia Zhijun at his temporary residence, seizing on the spot one imitation Type 64 pistol, 3 rounds of ammunition, 78.64 grams of white powder containing ketamine, and 611.33 grams of light yellow powder containing ephedrine.

In summary, Defendants Xia Zhijun and He Pingquan, together with others, engaged in four separate acts of manufacturing ketamine, producing a total of over 320 kilograms of ketamine, of which over 280 kilograms were seized after the case came to light.

(2) Judgment

The court held that Defendants Xia Zhijun, He Pingquan, Xu Xiangping, He Fangming, Chen Yong, Yang Cuibin, and You Chao, in violation of drug control regulations, illegally produced ketamine, and their acts constituted the crime of manufacturing drugs. Defendant Wang Ping, knowing that others were manufacturing drugs, provided drug-manufacturing equipment and raw materials, and his act also constituted the crime of manufacturing drugs. Xia Zhijun and He Pingquan also, in violation of firearms control regulations, illegally possessed firearms with lethal capability, and their acts each further constituted the crime of illegal possession of firearms. In the joint crime of manufacturing drugs, Xia Zhijun, He Pingquan, and Xu Xiangping were principals and should be punished for all crimes in which they participated or which they organized or directed; He Fangming, Chen Yong, Yang Cuibin, You Chao, and Wang Ping played secondary or auxiliary roles, were accessories, and should be given a lighter punishment according to law. Xia Zhijun and He Pingquan manufactured over 320 kilograms of ketamine, an extraordinarily large quantity; moreover, part of the drugs had already entered society, causing great social harm, with extremely serious crimes; they also illegally possessed firearms; they should be punished according to law and subjected to cumulative punishment for multiple crimes. Xia Zhijun had previously been sentenced for robbery, and within five years after completing that sentence, he committed another crime punishable by fixed-term imprisonment or above; he was a recidivist with deep subjective malignancy and high personal danger, and should be given a heavier punishment according to law. With respect to He Pingquan's crime of illegal possession of firearms, he voluntarily surrendered himself, so he could be given a lighter punishment for that crime according to law. You Chao was also a recidivist and should be given a heavier punishment according to law. Accordingly, Defendants Xia Zhijun and He Pingquan were sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; Defendant Xu Xiangping was sentenced to death, with a two-year suspension of execution; Defendants He Fangming, Chen Yong, Yang Cuibin, and You Chao were each sentenced to life imprisonment; and Defendant Wang Ping was sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment.

2. Wang Zhengyuan, Zhu Yufeng, et al. — Smuggling and transporting drugs

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Wang Zhengyuan, male, Han nationality, born December 7, 1965, unemployed. In September 1983, he was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for robbery; in May 1991, he was sentenced to four years and six months' imprisonment for theft; in August 1996, he was sentenced to five years and six months' imprisonment for theft; and he was released upon completion of sentence on August 29, 2001.

Defendant Zhu Yufeng, male, Han nationality, born December 8, 1978, farmer.

Defendant Zhai Jianhai, male, Han nationality, born February 17, 1979, unemployed.

Defendant Hu Debiao, male, Han nationality, born April 17, 1976, farmer. In January 1997, he was sentenced to five years' imprisonment for theft, and was released upon completion of sentence on May 6, 2001.

Defendant Wang Ping, male, Han nationality, born August 17, 1974, farmer.

In early March 2008, Defendant Zhu Yufeng directed Shuai Jianfei (already separately convicted and sentenced) to smuggle drugs from Myanmar. Shuai Jianfei brought the drugs into the country and then, in Jinghong City, Yunnan Province, handed them over to Yin Shupeng (already separately convicted and sentenced), and instructed Yin to transport them by passenger bus to Kaiyuan City, Yunnan Province. At around 0:00 on March 10 of the same year, when the passenger bus was passing through a toll station in Ning'er County, Yunnan Province, public security officers seized 7,000 grams of methamphetamine from a travel bag carried by Yin Shupeng.

In early April of the same year, after Defendant Wang Zhengyuan organized a drug supply in Myanmar, Defendant Zhu Yufeng arranged for Sun Daguo (already separately convicted and sentenced) to take delivery of the drugs in Myanmar. On April 9 of the same year, Sun Daguo instructed others to transport the drugs into the country and, in Daluo Town, Menghai County, Yunnan Province, handed them over to Ma Shengxi (already separately convicted and sentenced), who was to transport them to Jinghong City. At 18:20 on the same day, Ma Shengxi was arrested in Daluo Town, and public security officers seized from his motorcycle 21.821 kilograms of methamphetamine.

In mid-May of the same year, Defendant Wang Zhengyuan arranged in Myanmar for Defendant Zhu Yufeng to have Sun Daguo transport the remaining drugs from the previous shipment into the country. On May 19 of the same year, Sun Daguo instructed others in Myanmar to hand over the drugs to Zhang Kefeng and Liu Lefeng (both already separately convicted and sentenced). Liu Lefeng rode a motorcycle ahead to scout the route, while Zhang Kefeng followed on a motorcycle carrying the drugs, heading toward Jinghong City. At approximately 21:53 on the same day, Zhang and Liu were arrested en route, and public security officers seized 5,430 grams of methamphetamine from the motorcycle ridden by Zhang Kefeng.

In late May of the same year, Defendant Wang Zhengyuan smuggled a batch of drugs into the country and asked Defendant Zhu Yufeng to send someone to take delivery in Kunming City, Yunnan Province, and then transport them to Wuhan City, Hubei Province. On June 2, Zhu Yufeng instructed Defendant Zhai Jianhai to go to Kunming City to receive the drugs, and on the afternoon of June 4, Zhai handed them over to Defendant Wang Ping, who had been brought by Defendant Hu Debiao. Hu then directed Wang Ping to hand over the drugs to Huang Xiaoqin (handled separately), who was with Wang Ping. Huang was to carry the drugs by passenger bus to Kaiyuan City, with Zhai Jianhai accompanying on the same bus to monitor. Subsequently, Zhai, Hu, Wang, and Huang were arrested at the Kunming City bus station, and public security officers seized 3,910 grams of methamphetamine from Huang Xiaoqin's shoulder bag. On July 10 of the same year, Zhu Yufeng was arrested in Lincang City, Yunnan Province.

On October 25 of the same year, Defendant Wang Zhengyuan hid drugs inside a women's shaping garment in Myanmar and had Zhang Shaoli (handled separately) give it to Cai Mingyi (a minor, already separately convicted and sentenced) to bring into the country and transport to Wuhan City, and instructed Yang Xiaoling (handled separately) to monitor Cai Mingyi. At approximately 15:00 on October 27 of the same year, when Cai and Yang were traveling by passenger bus and passing through the Wulong toll station on the Kunming-Qujing Expressway, they were arrested, and public security officers seized 910 grams of methamphetamine from Cai Mingyi's person.

On October 27 of the same year, Defendant Wang Zhengyuan hid drugs inside two shaping garments and had Zhang Shaoli bind the garments containing drugs to Li Ping (already separately convicted and sentenced) and Li Mei (handled separately), respectively, to bring them into the country and transport to Wuhan City, and arranged for Xiong Zhongbao (already separately convicted and sentenced) to monitor. At approximately 18:40 on October 28, when Li Ping and Li Mei were traveling by passenger bus and passing through the Xiaomengyang toll station in Jinghong City, they were arrested, and public security officers seized a total of 3,712.2 grams of methamphetamine from their persons. On October 30 of the same year, Wang Zhengyuan was arrested in Myanmar.

In summary, Defendant Wang Zhengyuan organized and directed the smuggling and transportation of a total of 35.7832 kilograms of methamphetamine over five separate occasions; Defendant Zhu Yufeng directed others to smuggle and transport a total of 38.161 kilograms of methamphetamine over four separate occasions. After the case came to light, a total of 42.7832 kilograms of methamphetamine was seized.

(2) Judgment

The court held that Defendants Wang Zhengyuan and Zhu Yufeng, in violation of drug control regulations, smuggled methamphetamine into the country and transported it, and their acts constituted the crimes of smuggling and transporting drugs. Defendants Zhai Jianhai, Hu Debiao, and Wang Ping, for the purpose of obtaining illegal benefits, transported methamphetamine, and their acts constituted the crime of transporting drugs. Wang Zhengyuan and Zhu Yufeng engaged in drug smuggling and transportation on multiple occasions, involving an extraordinarily large quantity of drugs, with extremely serious crimes and great social harm; moreover, they played primary roles in the joint crimes, and were principals, and should be punished for all crimes they organized or directed. Wang Zhengyuan also instigated and used a minor to smuggle and transport drugs; he had also been sentenced three times for crimes, evidencing deep subjective malignancy and high personal danger, and should be given a heavier punishment according to law. Zhai Jianhai, Hu Debiao, and Wang Ping transported a large quantity of drugs; in view of their relatively good attitude in admitting guilt after arrest, and that Wang Ping was an accessory, Zhai Jianhai and Hu Debiao were given a discretionary lighter punishment, and Wang Ping was given a mitigated punishment. Accordingly, Defendants Wang Zhengyuan and Zhu Yufeng were sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; Defendants Zhai Jianhai and Hu Debiao were each sentenced to life imprisonment; and Defendant Wang Ping was sentenced to eight years' imprisonment.

3. Liu Wei, et al. — Trafficking and manufacturing drugs

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Liu Wei, male, Han nationality, born February 6, 1970, unemployed. In February 1988, he was sentenced to seven years' imprisonment for hooliganism, and was released upon completion of sentence on October 13, 1994.

Defendant Yu Fei, male, Han nationality, born November 21, 1977, unemployed. In May 2005, he was sentenced to one year's imprisonment for drug trafficking, and was released upon completion of sentence on September 24, 2005.

Defendant Hou Ying, male, Han nationality, born March 23, 1964, worker.

Defendant Zhang Chaogang, male, Han nationality, born February 17, 1970, unemployed.

Defendant Nie Bing, male, Han nationality, born October 14, 1980, unemployed.

Defendant Guan Dexin, male, Manchu nationality, born June 8, 1964, unemployed. In March 2007, he was sentenced to six months' imprisonment for drug trafficking, and was released upon completion of sentence on May 29, 2007.

Defendant Liu Zhishun, male, Han nationality, born November 11, 1962, unemployed.

Defendant Gao Baopan (fán), male, Han nationality, born January 31, 1971, unemployed.

Defendant Zhang Jinlong, male, Hui nationality, born January 16, 1965, unemployed.

Defendant Liu Wei and Yu Fei conspired to manufacture a heroin dilution solution for profit. From November 2006 to August 2007, Liu Wei provided the funds, and together or with Yu Fei acting alone, they purchased a total of 1,050 grams of heroin on several occasions to be used in manufacturing the heroin dilution solution. Liu Wei first, together with Defendant Hou Ying, manufactured the heroin dilution solution in Yuhong District, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province, and later in Xinchengzi District hired Defendant Zhang Chaogang to bottle and seal the solution to produce injections. By the time the case was uncovered, Liu Wei and others had manufactured a total of 53,560 injections of heroin dilution solution (1.8 grams per injection, totaling 96.408 kilograms), 13 bottles of 600 ml solution (approximately 600 grams per bottle, totaling 7.8 kilograms), 2 barrels of solution in mineral water containers (17.7 kilograms), and 19 bottles of 2 liter solution (approximately 2 kilograms per bottle, totaling 38 kilograms), for a combined total of approximately 160 kilograms. Among these, Zhang Chaogang participated in manufacturing 2 barrels of heroin dilution solution (weighing 17.7 kilograms) and 47,560 injections.

From November 2006 to September 2007, in Shenyang City, Defendant Liu Wei sold to Defendant Yu Fei 20,500 injections of heroin dilution solution, 13 bottles of 600 ml heroin dilution solution (equivalent to approximately 3,900 injections), and 19 bottles of 2 liter heroin dilution solution (equivalent to approximately 19,000 injections); and sold to Zhou Wei and Jin Danping 5,000 and 17,000 injections of heroin dilution solution, respectively.

From July to August 2007, Defendant Liu Wei sold the manufactured heroin dilution solution to Defendant Yu Fei and introduced drug buyers to Yu Fei. In Shenyang City, Yu Fei sold 1,500, 1,000, 240, and 500 injections, respectively, to Jin Danping, Zhou Wei, Wang Hong, and Defendant Guan Dexin, and instructed Defendant Nie Bing to sell 960, 2,000, and 300 injections, respectively, to Jin Danping, Zhou Wei, and Guan Dexin.

From December 2006 to June 2007, in Shenyang City, Defendant Nie Bing sold a total of over 16,000 injections of heroin dilution solution on multiple occasions.

From July to September 2007, in Shenyang City, Defendant Guan Dexin sold a total of 800 injections of heroin dilution solution on three occasions.

In January 2007, Defendant Liu Zhishun twice sold a total of 80 grams of heroin to Defendant Yu Fei in Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province.

In May 2007, Defendant Liu Wei and Gao Baopan conspired to manufacture ketamine. After learning from the Internet that Defendant Zhang Jinlong had posted information offering to sell a method for manufacturing ketamine, Gao Baopan, with funding from Liu Wei, went to Yinchuan City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, to learn the ketamine manufacturing technique from Zhang Jinlong. Based on this, Gao Baopan manufactured 1,540 grams of ketamine.

(2) Judgment

The court held that Defendants Liu Wei and Yu Fei, in violation of drug control regulations, joined to manufacture a heroin dilution solution and then trafficked it; Liu Wei also joined with others to manufacture ketamine; their acts constituted the crime of trafficking and manufacturing drugs. Defendants Hou Ying, Zhang Chaogang, and Gao Baopan joined others in illegally manufacturing drugs, and their acts constituted the crime of manufacturing drugs. Defendants Liu Zhishun, Nie Bing, and Guan Dexin illegally trafficked drugs, and their acts constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Defendant Zhang Jinlong taught others criminal methods for manufacturing drugs, and his act constituted the crime of teaching criminal methods. Liu Wei, together with others, trafficked and manufactured a large quantity of drugs; he was a principal in the joint crime; he had previously been sentenced for crimes, with deep subjective malignancy and high personal danger, and his crimes were extremely serious; he should be punished according to law. Yu Fei, together with others, trafficked and manufactured a large quantity of drugs; he was a principal in the joint crime; he was also a recidivist and a drug repeat offender, and should be given a heavier punishment according to law. However, in view that his role in the joint crime was relatively less than that of Liu Wei, the death penalty imposed on him did not need to be immediately executed. Hou Ying, Zhang Chaogang, and Gao Baopan, in joining others, manufactured a large quantity of drugs; they were principals in the joint crime, and should each be punished for all crimes in which they participated. Nie Bing trafficked a large quantity of drugs and was a principal in the joint crime; in view of his voluntary surrender and his meritorious performance in assisting in the arrest of co-defendant Guan Dexin, his punishment could be mitigated according to law. Guan Dexin trafficked a large quantity of drugs and was a recidivist and a drug repeat offender, and should be given a heavier punishment according to law. Liu Zhishun trafficked a large quantity of drugs, and should be punished according to law. Zhang Jinlong, for profit, used the Internet to post information offering to sell a method for manufacturing drugs, and taught Gao Baopan the specific method for manufacturing ketamine; based on this, Gao manufactured 1,540 grams of ketamine; this was a serious crime, and Zhang should be punished according to law. Accordingly, Defendant Liu Wei was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; Defendant Yu Fei was sentenced to death, with a two-year suspension of execution; Defendants Hou Ying, Zhang Chaogang, and Gao Baopan were sentenced to life imprisonment, fifteen years' imprisonment, and fifteen years' imprisonment, respectively; Defendants Liu Zhishun, Nie Bing, and Guan Dexin were sentenced to fifteen years', fourteen years', and ten years' imprisonment, respectively; and Defendant Zhang Jinlong was sentenced to five years' imprisonment.

4. Li Dezhong, et al. — Trafficking drugs and illegal possession of firearms

(1) Basic Facts

Defendant Li Dezhong, male, Han nationality, born September 22, 1965, unemployed.

Defendant Xia Shiyun, male, Han nationality, born September 19, 1974, unemployed. In December 1994, he was sentenced to thirteen years' imprisonment for theft, and was released upon completion of sentence on June 18, 2003.

Defendant Ma Zhongfu, male, Han nationality, born July 23, 1975, unemployed. In August 1994, he was sentenced to eight years' imprisonment for theft and robbery, and was released upon completion of sentence on May 22, 1998.

From October 2007 to April 2008, Defendant Li Dezhong, together with Gu Xiaojuan (deceased), purchased "K powder" (ketamine) from Chengdu City, Sichuan Province. The seller shipped the drugs via a logistics company to Shishi City, Fujian Province, where Li retrieved them and trafficked them locally. Li Dezhong and Gu Xiaojuan successively hired Defendants Xia Shiyun and Ma Zhongfu to retrieve and sell "K powder" to others. Among these, Xia Shiyun retrieved a total of 8,000 grams of "K powder" over three occasions, and Ma Zhongfu retrieved a total of 17,000 grams of "K powder" over eight occasions. Most of this "K powder" was sold; upon case resolution, 238 grams of "K powder" was seized from Xia Shiyun's rental residence, and 5,100 grams of "K powder" was seized from Ma Zhongfu's rental residence.

In late March 2008, through contact by Defendant Li Dezhong, Defendant Xia Shiyun went to Chongqing City and purchased 450 grams of cannabis, which he brought back to Shishi City. Xia, together with Defendant Ma Zhongfu, mixed the cannabis into cigarettes and repackaged them as cannabis cigarettes. Apart from a portion that was sold, 100 grams of cannabis shreds was seized after the case was uncovered.

On April 8, 2008, when Peng Fangjian (handled separately) was shipping from a logistics company in Chengdu City 2,000 grams of "K powder" that Li Dezhong had purchased, public security officers seized it on the spot.

On April 11, 2008, when Defendant Ma Zhongfu went to a logistics company in Shishi City to retrieve "K powder" that Li Dezhong had purchased, he was arrested. Public security officers seized on the spot 5,100 grams of "K powder" and 197.3 grams of methamphetamine.

Since June 2007, the defendant Li Dezhong secretly kept a replica "Type 64" pistol and 3 rounds of ammunition at his rental residence in Shishi City. At the end of December 2007, Li Dezhong handed over the pistol and ammunition to Xia Shiyun for concealment, which were later seized.

In summary, the defendant Li Dezhong trafficked 32,100 grams of ketamine, 197.3 grams of methamphetamine, and 450 grams of cannabis. Upon the case being uncovered, 12,438 grams of ketamine, 197.3 grams of methamphetamine, and 100 grams of cannabis cigarettes were seized.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendants Li Dezhong, Xia Shiyun, and Ma Zhongfu, for the purpose of profit, illegally trafficked ketamine, methamphetamine, cannabis, and other drugs, and their actions all constituted the crime of drug trafficking. Li Dezhong and Xia Shiyun also violated firearms control regulations by illegally possessing lethal firearms, and their actions further constituted the crime of illegal possession of firearms. Li Dezhong trafficked a huge quantity of drugs, played a principal role in the joint crime, and was a principal offender. He also illegally possessed firearms, showing deep subjective malice and high personal dangerousness, and the crimes were extremely serious. He should be punished according to law and subjected to concurrent punishment for multiple crimes. Xia Shiyun and Ma Zhongfu trafficked a huge quantity of drugs, played a secondary role in the joint crime as accomplices, and should be given a lighter punishment according to law. Xia Shiyun had previously been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment or heavier punishment for a crime, and within five years after his release from prison, he again committed a crime punishable by fixed-term imprisonment or heavier punishment, making him a recidivist. He also illegally possessed firearms and should be given a heavier punishment according to law and subjected to concurrent punishment for multiple crimes. Ma Zhongfu assisted the public security organs in capturing Li Dezhong after being brought to justice, constituting a major meritorious service, and could be given a lighter punishment according to law. Accordingly, the defendant Li Dezhong was sentenced to death and the death penalty was approved; the defendant Xia Shiyun was sentenced to death, with a two-year suspension of execution; and the defendant Ma Zhongfu was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 15 years.
